e: The House of Representatives decides to end Aguila Saleh Issa's role as speaker.
Teachers go on strike, demanding a pay raise, delaying the start of school.
The country’s two rival governments reach an initial agreement to overhaul the electoral system.
Seven migrants are found dead after a charity rescue ship rescues 50 others from a wooden boat in international waters off Libya; the survivors claim to have had departed Zuwara the previous day.
An attack on the South Zawiya substation causes a complete power outage across wide areas south of Zawiya; more than 700 MW of the Zawiya power station’s 1,300 capacity remains unavailable.
A drone assault hits the Zawia Oil Refining Company for the third time in two days.
Fawzi al-Mansouri, commander of the Libyan National Army's intelligence branch, is assassinated in a car bombing outside his home in Benghazi.

Mohammed Takala is re-elected as Head of the High Council of State with 80 votes out of 136. Naji Mukhtar is elected as First Deputy Speaker with 69 votes, Omar Dabushah as Second Deputy Speaker and Belgassem Dabraz as Rapporteur with 70 votes.
Protests break out in Tripoli over an electricity crisis and deteriorating standard of living.
The United States imposes a 12.5% tariff on Libya, citing the presence of alleged forced labour in the supply chain.

The eastern-based Government of National Stability led by Osama Hammad bans the entry of nationals from Sudan, Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Somalia, citing a reorganization of foreign nationals' entry procedures.
Ossama Anjiem aka Ossama al-Masri, a warlord who led the Tripoli branch of the Reform and Rehabilitation Institution, is convicted for committing human rights violations on inmates at the facility.
The bodies of 15 migrants are discovered along the coast of Al-Khums.
A boat carrying migrants capsizes off eastern Libya, leaving 51 passengers dead or missing and 10 survivors.
A boat carrying migrants sinks off Tobruk, leaving 17 people dead, nine missing and seven rescued.
The Tripoli Criminal Court sentences four members of a human trafficking gang to between 12 and 22 years in prison for migrant smuggling, abduction, and torture.
The bodies of 17 migrants are recovered by authorities from the coast near Zuwarah.
The Russian tanker Arctic Metagaz is attacked by a suspected Ukrainian naval drone off the coast of Libya. All 30 crew are rescued.
Dozens of soldiers are killed in clashes in areas bordering Niger and Chad over several days during a joint operation affiliated with the Libyan National Army.
The bodies of five migrants are found washed up on the coast of Qasr al-Akhyar.
Libya grants oil exploration and production licences for the first time since 2009 to several foreign energy firms, including Chevron Corporation and Aiteo.
A medical helicopter crashes at the Maaten al-Sarra Air Base, killing all five occupants on board.
The United States says it has captured Zubayr Al-Bakoush, a key participant in the 2012 Benghazi attack.
A rubber boat carrying migrants capsizes off Zuwara, leaving 53 people dead or missing and only two survivors.
Three members of the Libyan National Army are killed in an attack along the border with Niger.
Libya signs a US$20 billion 25-year oil development deal with TotalEnergies and ConocoPhillips through Waha Oil Company.
At least 21 bodies of migrants are found in a mass grave near Ajdabiya. Up to 10 survivors show signs of torture, and a farm owner is arrested after admitting the presence of the grave.
